quest.title: The Final Question
quest.description: Seymour's lost data has been retrieved, but the scattered fragments must be put together as soon as possible. All possible connections must be attempted to complete the prototype's initial and final mission...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x150, Primogem x20, Mora x25000

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wh—What's going on? We seem to be in a different place now... But where is this?

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Searching... No data concerning this place has been found in my memory banks.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So you haven't been here before either, then?

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: #Affirmative. There is no need to worry, {M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME}, Ms. Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: I am equipped with the most advanced optics from the Fontaine Institute of Natural Philosophy. I simply need to record this information in my storage units and compare it with previous data...

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: The odds of this being the Narzissenkreuz Ordo are high.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: High... Guess this must be the place we're looking for, then!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So this is the Narzissenkreuz Ordo!

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Recording... This location and data regarding it have been recorded in my storage unit.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We've been here before... The Mary-Ann you're looking for probably isn't here...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But we might still find some clues that we didn't before.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Affirmative. I do not detect any possible source of danger.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, then you can just stay here for now, right?

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: A wise choice. The two of you should use your limited time more effectively.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Patience is a virtue in some situations, but meaningless waiting is merely a waste of time.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We'll come back to see you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, Mamere's gonna be super worried about you, too. You've gotta go back to her in one piece, after all!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Did you remember anything useful upon arriving here, Seymour?

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Negative. The newly-recorded information is pending further analysis and organization. No effective conclusion possible at present.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Then, uh, are we gonna have to wait for a long time until...

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Affirmative. Record space collation starting. Total time required, unknown. Interactive functions will cease temporarily while this is ongoing.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait! Hold on a second first!

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: #Roger. Interrupting space collation process. What instructions, {M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME}, Ms. Paimon?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Come to think of it, we don't know a lot about you either, Seymour.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: All we know is that your master isn't Mamere, but is someone named Mary-Ann.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Affirmative. Ms. Mary-Ann is my master. According to my standard deduction module, the odds of finding clues as to her whereabouts here are high.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We know, you said that before too. But it felt like there were some more basic questions we hadn't answered yet... Now seems like a good time, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If you could tell us a bit more about yourself and Mary-Ann, we might be able to better help you.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Of course, kind Miss.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #So, {NICKNAME}, what would you like to ask?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Any other questions?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Tell us about yourself, Seymour...

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: I am Prototype 4ACV07, designed by *garbled mechanical noises* to accompany and protect my master, Ms. Mary-Ann.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, Paimon didn't get a word of that.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: ...*garbled mechanical noises* is my creator.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: I am equipped with the most advanced optics, memory storage unit, logic unit, and various functional modules from the Fontaine Institute of Natural Philosophy.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uhh... That was clear as mud, but it sure sounds impressive...?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The more impressive the equipment, the harder it might be to fix once broken...

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Note: Regular record space collation can decrease the frequency of such issues effectively.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, basically... before you've done your collation thing, there's some stuff that you can't tell us even if you knew, right?

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Affirmative. More precisely, *garbled mechanical noises* grasped *garbled mechanical noises*.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Information regarding *garbled mechanical noises* can be extracted using *garbled mechanical noises*.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: This allows me to keep a log of Ms. Mary-Ann's daily life and also act as an agent's assistant.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are you serious? The important bits all got cut off!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What's an agent's assistant?

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: An "agent" refers to a member of the Marechaussee Phantom who undertakes investigations. In this context, "assistant" refers to "Seymour," prototype 4ACV07 itself.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So, Mary-Ann was a Marechaussee Phantom agent?

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Affirmative.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait. If that's who she is, wouldn't looking for official records help us find her faster? Why'd we need to come here?

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Ms. Mary-Ann's role as an agent was not publicized. Additionally, the case she investigated has to do with *garbled mechanical noises*.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: It is *garbled mechanical noises* performed at the direction of *garbled mechanical noises*. As such... *garbled mechanical noises*.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh, Seymour, you're breaking down again, aren't you?

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Note: Regular record space collation can decrease the frequency of such issues effectively.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's... just ask a different question, shall we...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Tell me about the Narzissenkreuz Ordo...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Can we really find clues about Mary-Ann's whereabouts here? You've never been here before, right? So why do you think we'll find clues here?

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: My latest records indicate that the last records before meeting Ms. Mamere were those of myself executing a specific process.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: This process was the capture of fugitive elements from the Narzissenkreuz Ordo. Ms. Mary-Ann was also executing this process.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: As her companion and guard, I followed her and *garbled mechanical noises* into Elynas.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: There, we encountered members of the Narzissenkreuz Ordo, including Jakob Ingold, a core member of said Ordo.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So he was a member? And Mary-Ann was pursuing him...

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Affirmative.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, guess there really was some relation there, then... Gah! We should've captured Jakob and questioned him.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon wonders if he'll come back here — if we ever meet again, we're gonna have questions for him.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: He doesn't seem like the sort who'll simply answer questions if asked.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If all else fails, we can just... y'know, go good-cop bad-cop on him! There's gotta be some way, or else we're stuck waiting for Seymour to recall stuff.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: You mean, when I complete my record space collation, Ms. Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Those things are basically the same!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Tell me about your latest records...

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: A fierce battle against the members of the Ordo broke out within Elynas. My storage unit encountered an error due to massive trauma.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: We must foil the Ordo's plans. To that end, Jakob Ingold, *garbled mechanical noises* ... *garbled mechanical noises* must be stopped.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Due to *garbled mechanical noises* ... *garbled mechanical noises* ... *garbled mechanical noises* ... to Ms. Mary-Ann.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You'd best take a break.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Your words are most considerate.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Seems like we're gonna have to wait for you to do that collation thing, Seymour...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But whatever the case, Jakob was trying to do something bad inside Elynas, while you and Mary-Ann were trying to stop him, right?

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Affirmative. Your summary is overly simplistic, perhaps, but it is basically the truth, Ms. Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If we only have this information...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Finding Mary-Ann might be somewhat difficult.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Doesn't seem like we've got other options beyond waiting for you to do that record collation of yours, Seymour.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Affirmative. My calculations indicate that this is the approach with the highest success rate.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But it'll take a lot of time, won't it?

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: If you wish, I can estimate the amount of time required. Processing time required... unknown.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, yeah, no need for this estimation stuff, then!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Well, Paimon's done asking Seymour questions now. But boy has she still got some for you, {NICKNAME}! You promised you'd explain, didn't you?

choices.text: I didn't stash any snacks away without your knowledge.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But there's no one to disturb us now, and Seymour's... Well, a related party, right? No time like the present, then!

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You tell Paimon and Seymour about the conversation you had previously with Elynas...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, so that's a thing that happened. Paimon thought you'd gotten sick or something when you started saying all that weird stuff!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, it's good to know that you're fine!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: By the way, Seymour, leaving you here to perform your record collation wouldn't be a problem, would it?

choices.text: There wasn't a good time to have this conversation earlier...

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: A new friend... oh? Actually, looks like an old friend.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Negative. Danger. Danger. Activity by Narzissenkreuz Ordo remnants detected.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: We meet again. What did the White Cavalier of Protection say about you? Ah, yes. "This is my little invention."

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Affirmative. I am... *garbled mechnical noises* prototype, with a large number of bold design elements.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: ...The priority level of this topic has been downgraded. Please lay down your arms and surrender.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: #Seymour, listen to me. I've already surrendered to {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Is that so?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yes, totally.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Very well. In that case, we can continue to discuss my extraordinary design.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: I am Caterpillar, as you know. Speaking of which, how's the young lady you were protecting doing?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: ...Wait a moment. Why did I say something like that?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: You are correct. I am looking for the master I should protect, Ma—

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Mary-Ann. Or, as you might call her, Mary-Ann Guillotin.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...Mary-Ann Guillotin!

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: ... *mechanical noises* ...*the mechnical noises slowly become clearer* Guillotin.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Correct. My designer. Guillotin.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Caterpillar, is this your memories from hundreds of years ago, y'know, getting clearer?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: No. This is a memory from before my birth, something akin to an elephant recalling its previous life while meditating.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: I do not understand. Previous lives do not exist.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Not for you, at least.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Thanks to you, it seems that I've encountered a potential breakthrough I had never imagined possible. Perhaps I might find the secrets to my own birth after all.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Though I do not understand, I am glad to have been of service.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: In that case, why don't we exchange information?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Since Seymour's here, maybe you'll be able to find some special records or something, Caterpillar.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: I do not understand, but I determine the likelihood of success to be high.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You share the information...

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: So, Jakob has emerged...

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: I have another hypothesis about all this, but to prove my conjecture, I still need to conduct some onsite investigations. If you could accompany us, Seymour, that would help a lot.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: This is a decision that will help restore my records. I will accompany you.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: #Very good. In that case... {NICKNAME}, Paimon, once I am 90% confident, I will inform you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Great!

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: *yawn*~

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Ann, you're awake!

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: #Oh... Good morning, Paimon, Knight {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh, yes, let Paimon introduce you. This is Ann, an Oceanid and a friend of ours. Ann, this is...

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: ...I know. You're the silly dog, Seymour.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: I lack the relevant data. I do not believe we have had the honor of meeting, Oceanid Ann.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: I've never met you before, either. But I was sure of it the moment I saw you — you must be Seymour.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, what's going on here?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: This must be... No, I don't know, either. I feel... strange...

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Note: Regular record space collation can decrease the frequency of such issues effectively.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Anyway, let's bring you up to speed...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You shed a little light on the matters so far...

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: So, Seymour is searching for Mary-Ann...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Agh! No wonder that name felt familiar! The person Seymour mentioned and is looking for is also named Mary-Ann!

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Note: Regular record space collation can decrease the frequency of such issues effectively.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmmm... According to what Seymour said before, they can't be the same Mary-Ann, right? The timing...

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Based on your statement, may I deduce that you have met someone named Mary-Ann in the past, or perhaps read or heard about such a person from sources apart from myself?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, that was her name, that's for sure. Y'know what, let's do it like this — we can call the Mary-Ann in the Annapausis "Mary-Ann 1," and the one you're looking for, Seymour, can be "Mary-Ann 2"!

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Negative. The Ms. Mary-Ann I am searching for is of a higher sequential priority. To prevent confusion, she should be "Mary-Ann 1" instead.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Huh? Why don't you look at it this way, Seymour. 2 is bigger than 1. Doesn't that make it pretty good, too?

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Your claim... Sorting data fragments.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Uh, looks like he's stopped functioning again...

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Hehe, silly dog.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh, Paimon didn't think you had any mean bones in you, Ann, but you sure do!

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Haha. I don't know why, but I suddenly felt compelled to do that...

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Preliminary data fragment sorting complete. For the following 15 reasons, Oceanid Ann, I assess that your perspective is illogical. Firstly—

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Alright, alright, that stuff doesn't matter. Come, good doggie, sit.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Understood.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: ...Why?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: If you sit, we'll be able to improve photo-taking stability, right?

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Yes. Do you need to take a photo, Oceanid Ann? I am equipped with the most advanced optics from the Fontaine Institute of Natural Philosophy. I can—

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Oh, there's no need, but thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Understood.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, Seymour's getting played left and right over here!

choices.text: Let's call a quick halt, please...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Really... Anyway, wanna go to the Annapausis, Seymour? That way, you can meet that "Mary-Ann" and see if she's the one you're looking for or not.

response.speaker: Paimon

choices.text: Do you want to go to the Annapausis, Seymour?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, Seymour's getting played left and right over here!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Can we pause for a second...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Still, when we first got here, Paimon couldn't help but notice... The clock here doesn't seem very accurate, does it?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Ah. That.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Simply put, it's the Doomsday Clock.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Doomsday Clock?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: When the clock strikes midnight, the apocalypse will come.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Doesn't this mean that the end of the world is almost upon us?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Huh, that really does take me back. When I was here before, they thought the apocalypse was still far away, and that though it wouldn't happen in our generation, we should stop it for the sake of the future.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: If the clock is accurate, then it is not far off now. Perhaps we shall lay ourselves down to sleep tonight, and the sun shall not rise in the morn. Perhaps the sea shall evaporate tomorrow.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Or perhaps we are already living in the apocalypse, and the good times have long ended.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! Get serious! Will the apocalypse really come?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: First, what we see is just a "clock," not the apocalypse itself. When it comes down to it, time is merely a tool humans use to measure changes in all forms of matter.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Narzissenkreuz was the one who used the "world-formula" to calculate the beginning of the end, and built this device.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: As such, I cannot answer your question, dear Paimon. Because this is all it is — a clock.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's true, huh...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Anyway, let's share our findings...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You and Paimon briefly share all that happened with the other three people (though technically speaking, none of them are humans).

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Input logged.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Elynas...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Did you think of something?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: I don't know. I'm not sure. It's like water boiling off into gas. I can't see it, and I can't quite grasp it, either.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh. Any thoughts or leads, Caterpillar?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Hmm... Can't say that I don't, but I'm still trying to sort some things out, so let's discuss this later.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Right. I kept forgetting to ask you something.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, I'm very grateful for everything you've done for Lanoire. So, is there anything that I can help you with?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Do you mean... anything? Just like making a wish?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Haha! It should be something within the scope of my abilities, of course. You did free Lanoire and I from prison, but I'm no Jinn in a bottle.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So, what would your wish be, Paimon?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, if that's the case, then Mora... No, wait, yummy food...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aah! There's so much that Paimon wants, but...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We've been having lots of fun traveling together, so we don't really need anything special. Instead, Caterpillar, can you help us help Ann and Seymour?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Paimon...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, what do you think? Is that a good wish?

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: I understand. Then, let us work together.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: #Now, I plan to work with Seymour and Ann to see if we can use our experiences and the information available here to figure something new out. {NICKNAME}, Paimon, let's meet back here later.
